insights.title: Data Quality Assessment
insights.text: The leads dataset contains 100,000 records across 14 fields. Data quality is excellent: 0 missing values, 0 duplicate Account IDs, 0 invalid Source values, and 0 invalid Deal Stage values were found. The dataset required no imputation or deduplication and was used as-is after standardisation of field names and creation of 8 derived features (source_tier, owner_freq, company_freq, notes_has_text, plus OHE columns).

insights.title: Pipeline Overview
insights.text: Across 100,000 total leads, 9,993 reached Closed Won — an overall win rate of 9.99%. A further 19,933 leads were Closed Lost or Disqualified (loss rate 19.94%), while 70,074 leads (70.1%) remain in active pipeline stages. The overall close rate (won + lost + disqualified) stands at 29.93%, suggesting substantial open pipeline with conversion potential still to be realised.

insights.title: Lead Source Performance
insights.text: Podcast is the highest-performing acquisition channel with a 10.69% win rate across 5,134 leads, followed by Partner Program (10.66%), Referral (10.59%), Webinars (10.56%), and Content Marketing (10.46%). The lowest-performing channel is Networking Event at 9.28%. The spread across all 20 sources is 1.41 percentage points — real but narrow. This spread is consistent across SQL validation and is not an artefact of data imbalance — all sources have approximately equal lead volumes (~5,000 each).

insights.title: Channel Group Analysis
insights.text: Grouping the 20 sources into 7 channel categories reveals that Referral / Partner delivers the highest win rate at 10.63% (10,070 leads). Events and Outbound channels both exceed 10%, while Other (9.52%) and Social Media (9.67%) underperform the 9.99% average. Inbound channels, despite the largest lead volume (25,012), achieve only 9.87% — a volume-quality trade-off worth monitoring. These patterns are actionable for budget allocation, though causation cannot be inferred from win rate differences alone.

insights.title: Notes Sentiment Analysis
insights.text: TextBlob sentiment analysis on the Notes field reveals that mean polarity scores are nearly identical across deal outcomes: Won = 0.0575, Lost = 0.0646, Open = 0.0621. The absolute difference between Won and Lost is only 0.0071 polarity points. This confirms that notes sentiment carries no meaningful signal for predicting deal outcomes in this dataset. The finding held across both EDA and permutation importance analysis (notes_sentiment permutation drop = +0.008953 — all near-zero).

insights.title: Predictive Model Performance (Phase 5)
insights.text: Three classifiers were trained to predict Closed Won (is_won=1) on a 70/15/15 stratified split (69,999 train / 15,001 val / 15,000 test) using 8 engineered features. Logistic Regression: val AUC = 0.5113, test AUC = 0.5166 (CV: 0.5003 ± 0.0054). Random Forest: val AUC = 0.505, test AUC = 0.5061 (CV: 0.5063 ± 0.0084). LightGBM: val AUC = 0.4963, test AUC = 0.4998 (CV: 0.5085 ± 0.0047). Best model: Logistic Regression (Val AUC = 0.5113), only 0.0113 above random baseline. High train AUC for RF (0.6525) and LGBM (0.6888) confirms overfitting — no generalizable signal exists in the available features.

insights.title: Feature Importance Interpretation (Phase 6)
insights.text: Random Forest Gini importance assigns 39.2% to notes_sentiment, followed by company_freq (22.7%) and notes_word_count (17.1%). However, permutation importance (actual ROC-AUC Δ when features are shuffled) shows near-zero impact: max = +0.008953 (notes_sentiment), min = -0.009671 (source). SHAP mean |SHAP| also confirms notes_word_count as the most influential feature (mean |SHAP| = 0.005713), but all absolute SHAP values are negligible. Gini importance overstates continuous features; no feature provides genuine predictive lift.

insights.title: Business Recommendations
insights.text: Based on validated analytical findings across all phases: (1) Prioritise Podcast, Partner Program, Referral, and Webinar channels — consistently above 10.5% win rates with Won:Lost ratios of 1.056–1.163. (2) Review Networking Event (9.28% win rate, Won:Lost = 0.909 — the only source with more losses than wins) and Website Form (9.29%) for conversion optimisation. (3) Inbound channels generate 24.7% of all Closed Won by volume despite average win rates — protect and scale this volume. (4) For predictive lead scoring, invest in capturing additional feature types: deal value, industry vertical, response time, engagement score, and follow-up count. Note: all recommendations are associations — causal claims require controlled experiments.

insights.title: Correlation vs Causation Statement
insights.text: All analytical findings in this project describe statistical associations observed in the dataset. The higher win rates for Podcast, Referral, and Partner Program sources reflect patterns in the data — they do not establish that these channels cause higher win rates. Unmeasured confounding factors (lead quality, industry, deal size, sales rep skill) may explain observed differences. Model coefficients and feature importances describe learned associations, not causal pathways. Business decisions based on these findings should be validated through controlled A/B experiments or quasi-experimental methods.
